msg: D-12: TBD-1 partially resolved — Shape A granularity chosen; body template still open (TBD-1b)

data.decision: TBD-1 partially resolved: spec granularity is Shape A (one requirement per file, concept index.md absorbing spec.yaml). The per-file body template remains open (TBD-1b): user finds the Volere-derived body unconventional; candidate conventions (EARS/Kiro, Gherkin, IEEE-29148-ish SRS, relabeled Volere) to be prototyped on the same real requirements before choosing.
data.rationale: User reviewed both shapes and preferred A, but flagged that even A reads unlike well-known spec structures; a convention prototype is needed to compare on real axes rather than labels.

msg: D-13: requirement template = hybrid (Shape A body + ears_pattern + verification_method); body-as-document focus

data.decision: Requirement files keep the shall + Why + Fit-criterion body and add ears_pattern and verification_method (Test|Inspection|Demonstration|Analysis) to frontmatter; optional ## Scenarios only for automatable sub-cases. Frontmatter stays minimal — the body is the document (mudissue focus).
data.rationale: Round-2 prototype: the security invariant broke pure EARS and made Gherkin misstate testability; relabeling Fit criterion as Acceptance loses precision.

msg: D-14: dogfooding eval loop adopted; single-design.md layout rejected — design docs follow design-system/Diataxis/MOC patterns

data.decision: Adopt the 7-signal dogfooding eval loop (tickets/s0-eval-design.md) with the ~2h minimal first slice. REJECT the single monolithic design.md: the design half of a concept is a folder of well-presented notes (concepts, flows, components with pen/visual embeds, dimensions/specs, usage, recipes) following recognized patterns — design-system component pages, Diataxis, Obsidian Maps of Content — to be surveyed and prototyped (round 4), not invented.
data.rationale: User: one design.md is not a readable pattern; reference existing patterns rather than invent.

msg: D-15: TBD-1 fully resolved — design half = round-4 folder IA (MOC + concepts/flows/components/recipes/reference, assets adjacent)

data.decision: TBD-1 and TBD-1b are resolved. Per concept: index.md + requirements/ (Shape A files, D-13 hybrid template) + design/ folder following the round-4 IA: _MOC.md curated map of content with reading path; concepts/ (Diataxis explanation, one mermaid + related requirements each); flows/ (one flow per note, diagram + step/actor/source table); components/ (Carbon-style pages: Anatomy, Variants, States, Specs, Usage, Related; assets/ adjacent, embedded via ![[…]]); recipes/ (Diataxis how-to with exact CLI); reference/ tables. decisions/ as MADR files and glossary.md per s0-design-research. TBD-2 (specs symlink) confirmed working in round 1 review.
data.rationale: User approved round-4 prototype ("looks great") after rejecting single design.md; every note type is borrowed from a recognized pattern (Carbon/GOV.UK/Polaris, Diataxis, Zettelkasten MOC, GDD, mudissue adjacency) — see tickets/s0-design-patterns.md.

msg: D1: All state to Markdown+frontmatter; seal survives as sidecar hash; contract files stay JSON

data.decision: All state converts to Markdown+frontmatter, including the run ledger and journal. Slices/events become files; the write-seal survives as a sidecar hash file (not a frontmatter key) so human edits in Obsidian do not invalidate machine trust. Claude Code contract files (plugin.json, hooks.json, model-registry.json) stay JSON — not our data model.
data.rationale: Uniform Markdown+frontmatter enables Obsidian-native editing and first-class wikilink navigation without sacrificing the write-seal integrity that groundwork depends on for enforcement. Contract files are tool-owned schemas, not motive data.

msg: D2: Per-session run collapsed into motive-scoped slice files with session+wave properties

data.decision: The per-session run is collapsed: slices are sub-issues of their motive (files/folders under the motive dir, mudissue-style <label>-<slug> naming) carrying session and wave properties; the advisor gate becomes one note per session under the motive; the Stop-gate queries slices by session property plus the session gate note verdict. Pacing counts distinct waves among this session slices.
data.rationale: Eliminating the separate run ledger JSON files unifies the data model and makes slices first-class Obsidian notes. Session and wave become queryable frontmatter properties rather than ledger-file indices.

msg: D3: Own implementation — no mudissue runtime dep; adopt gray-matter round-trip, patch-only writes, --json on every command

data.decision: Own implementation — no runtime dependency on mudissue. Adopt verbatim: gray-matter round-trip frontmatter parsing, patch-only-the-target-line property writes (Obsidian edits and CLI edits never clobber each other), wikilink formatting with escaping, --json on every command, generic primitives (cat/locate/get-property/set-property/append) plus typed bidirectional link commands.
data.rationale: A runtime dependency on mudissue would couple groundwork release cadence to an external project and make the install surface more complex. Adopting the patterns verbatim captures all the value while keeping groundwork self-contained.

msg: D4: TypeScript+Bun single gw binary; hooks become one-line shims; one shared Zod schema

data.decision: TypeScript compiled with Bun to a single gw binary; hooks become one-line shims invoking gw hook <name>; kills the .mjs/.d.mts split; one shared Zod schema for frontmatter across CLI and hooks. Plugin (hooks/skills/agents) remains the delivery and enforcement surface; a gw mcp server mode is a later, optional slice.
data.rationale: A single compiled binary eliminates the .mjs/.d.mts maintenance burden and gives hooks a stable, typed entrypoint. Bun compiles TypeScript natively without a separate tsc step. Zod schemas shared across CLI and hooks prevent the seam drift that causes parity failures.

msg: D5: Migration durable-artefacts-only via gw migrate; ephemeral state NOT migrated; parallel dir until cutover

data.decision: Migration is durable-artefacts-only via gw migrate: motive charters, tickets, journal decisions/TBDs. Ephemeral run state (per-session ledgers, seals, struggle tallies, open-items) is NOT migrated. New layout lives in a parallel directory until cutover so existing hooks keep working.
data.rationale: Migrating ephemeral state would risk losing data or corrupting live sessions. A parallel-directory approach lets the old path stay hot during development, enabling a clean cutover without a flag day.

msg: D6: Behavior-preserving is the acceptance baseline; all workflow changes deferred as TBRs

data.decision: Behavior-preserving is the acceptance baseline: on identical inputs the new stop-gate/pacing/guards make identical decisions to today's. ALL workflow changes — link-driven auto-blocked status, promoter phase, configurable status lists — are deferred to post-migration follow-ups (record as TBRs).
data.rationale: Bundling behavior changes with a format migration multiplies the risk surface and makes parity testing ambiguous. A clean behavior-identical cutover lets parity be machine-verified; workflow improvements become independent follow-up motives.

msg: D7: Obsidian vault = .groundwork/; configurable tracker path; spec cross-links via symlink with relative-link fallback

data.decision: Obsidian vault = .groundwork/ (the tracker dir), with a mudissue-style configurable tracker path so it can live outside the repo. Spec cross-links via a .groundwork/specs -> ../doc/specs symlink; fallback if symlink-following proves unreliable is CLI-emitted relative Markdown links.
data.rationale: Keeping the vault at .groundwork/ requires no repo restructuring and aligns with the existing tracker-dir convention. A symlink for specs enables wikilink navigation from motive notes to requirements without duplicating the doc/specs tree; the relative-link fallback handles Obsidian setups where symlink traversal is unreliable.

msg: D8: Specs to prose-first Markdown with frontmatter metadata; spec.yaml and _generated/ deleted; coverage via verifies wikilinks

data.decision: Specs move to mudissue-style human-readable shape: concept metadata absorbed into the concept's index.md frontmatter; requirements as prose-first Markdown with machine-facing bits (id, criticality, verification, status) in frontmatter; spec.yaml, constraints.md, and doc/specs/_generated/ are deleted; coverage becomes verifies: [[<req-id>]] wikilinks on slices (backlinks pane = coverage report). Exact file granularity is TBD-1.
data.rationale: Machine-generated _generated/ and spec.yaml are implementation details that obscure the human-readable requirements. Moving metadata to frontmatter makes requirements standalone documents that read cleanly in Obsidian and in a text editor. Wikilink coverage replaces a generated coverage report with a live backlinks view.

msg: Slices fenced by file ownership, not by acceptance criterion

data.decision: Wave-2 slices (S2-CLI, S2-MOTIVE, S2-SLICE) each own a disjoint src/gw subtree and all import the S1-SCHEMA Zod types; S1-SCHEMA is a mandatory tracer bullet and no wave-2 slice may define a frontmatter type.
data.rationale: Fencing a shared data model by acceptance criterion makes each implementer define its own frontmatter type and validate only its own branch. That shape is behind three prior defects in this repo. File-ownership fencing removes the race on an undefined type.
alternatives: Fence wave-2 slices by AC-1/AC-2/AC-4 and let each define the frontmatter it needs
Single sequential slice for the whole store layer, no parallelism

msg: Parity corpus captured from legacy hooks before any new implementation lands

data.decision: S0-PARITY-CORPUS runs in wave 0, before the S1-SCHEMA tracer bullet, recording full hook stdin payloads plus observed exit codes from the legacy path as committed fixture data.
data.rationale: AC-3 requires replaying identical inputs against old and new. Once legacy code is deleted at S6-CUTOVER the legacy verdicts are unrecoverable, so the corpus must be recorded while the old path still runs. Storing full payloads rather than summaries lets the parity suite execute both surfaces instead of asserting on source text.
alternatives: Capture the corpus after the new implementation lands, deriving expected verdicts from the spec
Skip recorded corpus and hand-write parity expectations from PACING-R-001..011 prose

msg: Spec migration blocked on the TBD-1 user decision point

data.decision: S4-SPEC-MIGRATE is blocked_by S0-PROTO, which ends at an explicit user decision resolving TBD-1 (file granularity) and TBD-2 (Obsidian symlink following). No spec file under doc/specs is modified before that decision.
data.rationale: The charter states spec migration is blocked on TBD-1. Committing to a granularity before reviewing both shapes in Obsidian would make the 55-requirement migration a rework risk. TBD-2 rides the same prototype because the symlink question is only answerable by opening the vault.
alternatives: Pick requirement-per-file up front on mudissue precedent and skip the prototype
Migrate one concept live and iterate in place
